memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'Anyone who touches anything she sits on must wash their clothes and bathe with water, and they will be unclean till evening. Whether it is the bed or anything she was sitting on, when anyone touches it, they will be unclean till evening.'" - Lev 15:22-23 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
When anyone touches it. There is no exemption for not knowing. A person could sit down without a thought and be ceremonially unclean before they stood up again.

That may feel unfair. But it teaches something true: reality is not governed by our awareness of it. A thing does not become harmless because we did not notice it.

We would often prefer otherwise. We would like our unintentional damage not to count — the words we did not realise were cutting, the neglect we did not notice, the prejudice we absorbed without examining it. But the person we hurt was still hurt, whether we meant it or not.

Scripture takes unintentional sin seriously enough to legislate for it. Leviticus has whole sections on offerings for sins committed unknowingly (Lev 4:2). David prayed: who can discern their own errors? Forgive my hidden faults (Ps 19:12).

That is a wise prayer, because it admits we cannot audit ourselves completely. There are things we get wrong that we will never spot.

And here is the relief: Christ's atonement covers what we know and what we do not. You do not need a complete inventory of your failures to be fully forgiven. He knows the whole list, and He has already dealt with it.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have you caused harm you did not intend and never addressed?
2. Can you pray honestly for God to reveal your hidden faults?
3. What comfort is there in Christ covering what you cannot even see?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, search me for the faults I cannot see in myself. Thank You that Christ's forgiveness covers not only what I know but what I have never noticed. Amen.
